paper.title: Clustering Items through Bandit Feedback: Finding the Right Feature out of Many

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit clustering of items with two groups (fixed confidence)
unmapped: Arms are (item, feature) pairs of an n x d mean matrix whose rows take one of two unknown vectors mu^a != mu^b (hidden two-group partition); goal is to recover the partition
learner knows the number of items n
settings.definition_quote: At each time step $t$, based on passed observation, the learner selects one item $I_t\in[n]$ and one question $J_t\in[d]$, then she receives $X_t$, a noisy evaluation of $M_{I_t,J_t}$. ... For a prescribed probability of error $\delta$, the learner's objective is to recover the groups with a probability of error not exceeding $\delta$, while minimizing the number of observations.

settings.name_in_paper: Bandit clustering of items with two groups (lower bound, Gaussian environments)
unmapped: Arms are (item, feature) pairs of an n x d mean matrix whose rows take one of two unknown vectors (hidden two-group partition); goal is to recover the partition
learner knows the number of items n
settings.definition_quote: We consider $\mathcal{E}_{per}(M)$ as the set of Gaussian environments constructed from $M$ by permuting rows and columns.

symbols.theta_bal: balancedness: proportion of items in the smallest group
symbols.Delta_norm_sq: squared Euclidean norm of the gap vector mu^a - mu^b
symbols.G_min: min over s in [d] of (d/s + n)(1/Delta_(s)^2 + 1), Delta_(s) the s-th largest gap entry in absolute value

conditions: two nonempty groups with distinct mean vectors

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With a probability of at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:cluster} returns $\hat g=g$ with a budget of at most $T\leqslant \tilde C\cdot \log\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)\cdot H$, where ... $\tilde{C}$ is a logarithmic factor smaller than $C \cdot \left(\log\log(1/\delta)\vee 1\right)^4 \cdot\log(dn)^5\log(d)(\log_+\log (1/\Delta_{(\tilde{s})}^2) \vee 1)$

results.notes: Log factor tilde C = C (loglog(1/delta) v 1)^4 log(dn)^5 log(d)(log+ log(1/Delta_(tilde s)^2) v 1) hidden in O_tilde. Correctness and budget hold jointly w.p. >= 1-delta.

symbols.theta_bal: balancedness: proportion of items in the smallest group
symbols.Delta_norm_sq: squared Euclidean norm of the gap vector
symbols.h: common nonzero value of the gap entries, Delta in {0,h}^d

source.label: cor:simplecase
source.quote: For $\delta\in (0,1/e)$ and $\Delta\in \{0,h\}^d$ with $0<h<1$, with a probability of at least $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:cluster} returns $\hat g=g$ with a budget of at most $\tilde{C} \cdot \log(1/\delta)\cdot\left(\frac{d}{\theta \Vert \Delta\Vert^2}+\frac{n}{h^2}\right)$, where $\tilde{C}$ is a logarithmic factor smaller than $C \cdot \left(\log\log(1/\delta)\vee 1\right)^4 \cdot\log(dn)^5(\log_+\log (1/h^2) \vee 1)$

results.notes: Log factor tilde C hidden in O_tilde.

symbols.Delta_norm_sq: squared Euclidean norm of the gap vector

conditions: sub-task: output an item from the other group than item 1 (not the full clustering)

source.label: thm:cr
source.quote: Let $\delta\in(0,1/e)$. Then, with probability larger than $1-\delta$, Algorithm~\ref{alg:cr}-- $\texttt{CR}(\delta)$ --returns an index $\hat i_{c}$, such that it holds that $\mu_{\hat i_c}\neq \mu_1$, and moreover the total budget is upper bounded by $\tilde{C} \cdot \log\left(\frac{1}{\delta}\right)\cdot \frac{d} {\theta}\left(\frac{1}{\Vert \Delta\Vert^2}+\frac{1}{s^*}\right)$

results.notes: Guarantee for the first sub-step (find an item of the second group), mapped to the clustering setting; tilde C = C(loglog(1/delta) v 1)^4 log(dn)^5 log(d)(log+log(1/Delta_(s*)^2) v 1).

symbols.G_min: min over s in [d] of (d/s + n)(1/Delta_(s)^2 + 1)

conditions: an item i_c with mu_{i_c} != mu_1 is given to the algorithm

source.label: thm:cbc
source.quote: Let $\delta\in (0,1/e)$, let $i_c\in[n]$ such that $\mu_{i_c}\neq \mu_1$. Then Algorithm~\ref{alg:cbc}-- \texttt{CBC}$(\delta,i_c)$ --returns $\hat g = g$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, with a budget of at most $\tilde C\cdot \log(1/\delta)\cdot  \min_{s\in[d]} \left[\left(\frac{d}{s}+n\right)\left(\frac{1}{\Delta_{(s)}^2}+1\right)\right]$

results.notes: Requires a representative of the second group as input; tilde C = C(loglog(1/delta) v 1)^4 log(d)^5 log+log(1/Delta_(tilde s)^2).

symbols.Delta_norm_sq: squared Euclidean norm of the gap vector

conditions: algorithm is delta-PAC for the clustering task
holds for some environment in the set of row/column permutations of M
bound on the (1-delta)-quantile of the budget: P(T >= bound) >= delta

source.label: Thm:LB
source.quote: Fix $\delta\in(0,1/4)$. Assume that $\mathcal{A}$ is $\delta$-PAC for the clustering task, then, there exists $\tilde\nu\in \mathcal E_{per}(M)$ such that the $(1-\delta)$-quantile of the budget of algorithm $\mathcal{A}$ is bounded as follows $\mathbb{P}_{\mathcal{A},\tilde\nu}\left(T\geqslant \frac{2(n-2)}{\Delta_{(1)}^2} \log\left(\frac{1}{4.8\delta}\right) \vee \frac{2d}{\theta\|\Delta\|_2^2}\log \frac{1}{6\delta}\right) \geqslant \delta$

results.notes: Quantile lower bound (T exceeds bound with prob >= delta). Second term also stated separately as Lemma E.1 (not recorded separately).

conditions: algorithm is delta-PAC for the clustering problem

source.label: lemma:LB2
source.quote: Assume that $\delta<1/2$. If $\mathcal{A}$ is $\delta$-PAC for the clustering problem, then for any environment $\nu$, $\mathbb{E}_{\mathcal{A},\nu}[T] \geqslant \frac{2(n-2)}{\Delta_{(1)}^2} \log\left(\frac{1}{2.4\delta}\right)$
